literal: Enduring life protecting, to those who practice compassion, there is not, they say, one's own life fearing action.
translation: They say that for those who protect all enduring life and practice compassion, there are no deeds or consequences that their own life need fear.
modern: நிலைபெற்ற உயிர்களைக் காப்பாற்றி அருளை ஆள்பவர்களுக்கு, தன் உயிர் அஞ்சும்படியான துன்பம் தரும் வினைகள் இல்லை என்று கூறுவர்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the protective power of compassion. The poet states that those who cherish and protect the enduring lives of other creatures (மன் உயிர்) and practice compassion (அருள்) will never experience terrifying consequences. The word 'வினை' here refers to harmful deeds or the painful karmic consequences that cause dread to one's own soul. The wise assert (என்ப) that such fear-inducing distress does not exist (இல்) for a compassionate person, as their benevolence acts as an ultimate shield.
